## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A 36-juan continuation of the *Jǐngdé chuándēng lù* covering Chán masters from the early eleventh century down to the mid-fourteenth, compiled anonymously in the very early Míng and included in the Nánzàng 南藏 and subsequent canonical collections. Traditional secondary attribution to the Míng monk [居頂](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%B1%85%E9%A0%82) Jūdǐng (d. 1404) is found in later catalogues but is not securely established in contemporary sources.

**Abstract**

Structurally a direct continuation of the *Jǐngdé* format, covering the Sòng, Jīn, and Yuán periods. The coverage of the later Sòng overlaps extensively with the *Liándēng huìyào* 聯燈會要 ([KR6q0008](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0008)) and *Jiātài pǔdēng lù* 嘉泰普燈錄 ([KR6q0010](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6q/KR6q0010)), which the *Xù chuándēng lù* silently incorporates; but it also treats the Yuán-era Línjì and Cáodòng masters who fell outside those earlier Sòng-era compilations.

The work entered the official canon through the 南藏 (Nánzàng) printed under the Míng Hóngwǔ emperor and was incorporated into the standard Chán canonical section of all subsequent canonical editions. Its anonymous character and its compositive editorial method (heavily drawing on earlier lamp records) reduce its independent source-value compared to the individual Sòng lamp records, but for Yuán-era Chán figures it is often the earliest available source.
